2. Facts relevant for disposal of the appeal are that present Respondent Nos.1-11 as plaintiffs filed Other Class Suit No.73 of 1997 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Betagi, Barguna, impleading the present petitioners and others as defendants for partition of the suit land, contending inter-alia, that 7 acres of land of C.S. Khatian No.559 of Mouja-Talusi Baria, Thana and District Barguna originally belonged to Someruddin and Sher Ali in equal share; The arrear of rent of the aforesaid land was due as such Rent Suit No.229 of 1948 was instituted and the same was decreed; Execution Case No.226 of 1949 was filed and the land was put in auction on 12.07.1949; One Arshed Ali purchased the said land in auction who sold 6.88 acres of land to Haji Hachonuddin Talukder, Tajem Ali and Sekander Ali by a registered sale deed on 27.02.1951 and handed over possession thereto; Rest 12 decimals of land was in possession of Arshed Ali who died leaving one son Mohammad Ali and one daughter Dholai Bibi; Haji Hachaonuddin Talukder sold 86 decimals of land under R.S. Khatian No.54 by a registered sale deed to Samertoban Bibi on 27.03.1954; Mohabbat Ali Kha died leaving 3 sons and one daughter namely Joynal Kha, Plaintiff No.6 Salim Kha, Defendant No.41 Sohrab Kha and Piyara Begum; Said Piyara Begum died leaving husband Defendant No.3 Kanchon Ali Kha and son Defendant No.5 Belal; One Kashem Ali Kha took settlement of 65 decimals land from purchaser Haji Hachonuddin Talukder on 22.12.1952; Kashem Ali Kha sold the land on 05.11.1955 to Hatem Ali, Yousuf Ali and Hochen Ali by a registered sale deed and they sold 38 decimals of land to Tajem Ali and Sekander Ali by a registered sale deed; Hatem Ali sold 49 decimals of land under S.A. Khatian No.955 on 29.09.1951 to Mominuddin Kha, Entajuddin Kha and Afezuddin Kha; Entajuddin Kha, Mofez Kha, Rahima Bibi, Ambia and Halima Khatun sold 49 decimals of land of S.A. Khatian No.955 to Zulmat Kha on 30.04.1975; Defendant No.41 Sohrab Kha sold 13 decimals of land to Plaintiff No.2 Moslem Ali Kha who again sold the same to Defendant No.3 Kanchon Ali Kha on 12.05.1979; Haji Hachonuddin Talukder sold 6 decimals of land of S.A. Khatian No.955 to the predecessor of the plaintiff Mohabbat Ali Kha, Atahar Ali Kha, Amina Khatun and Samertaban Bibi on 27.03.1954; Haji macnonuaain Talukder died leaving two sons Defendant No.53 Hatem Ali, Yousuf Ali and 5 daughters Poribanu, Kodbanu, Iful Bibi, Rupshon Bibi and Rizia Khatun and wife Defendant No.50 Joynab Bibi; Rupshon Bibi died leaving one son Mohammad Ali and one daughter Dholai Bibi; Mohammad Ali and Dholai Bibi jointly inherited 12 decimals of land from their father and 24 decimals of land of S.A. Khatian No.955 from mother and jointly sold the same i.e. 36 decimals of land to Plaintiff Nos.2/5/6 on 24.03.1985; Atahar Ali Kha died leaving Plaintiff Nos.8-10 as heirs; Plaintiff Nos.9 and 10 sold 31 decimals of land to the Plaintiff Nos.2 and 12; Samertoban Bibi sold her entire share to Plaintiff Nos.3 and 4; Son of Haji Hachonuddin Talukder i.e. Yousuf Ali sold 1.19 acres of land to Defendant No.36 Yousuf Ali Munshi, Nurali and Abdur Razzak on 02.10.1963; Against the said transfer Mohabbat Ali Kha, Amina Khatun, Arabia Khatun and Atahar Ali Kha filed Preemption Case No.136/1964 under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and obtained order of preemption on 19.11.1965 from the 1st Munsif Court of Patuakhali; Yousuf Ali died leaving mother Defendant No.50 Joynab Bibi, two wives Defendant Nos.] and 51 Maleka Begum and Kulsum Bibi respectively, one son Defendant No.49 Abdus Sobhan and one daughter Defendant No.52 Farida Begum; Hatem Ali son of Haji Hachonuddin Talukder sold 65 decimals of land to Danesh Ali and Moslem Ali Kha on 08.11.1955; Against the said transfer father of Plaintiff No.6 Mohabbat Ali Kha, Atahar Ali Kha, Amina Khatun, Art bia Khatun and Samertoban Bibi filed Pre-emption Case No.164/1959 under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and obtained order of pre-emption on 23.01.1960 in which Plaintiff Nos.6-8 jointly got 45 decimals of land; Purchaser Sekander Ali died leaving son Adorn Ali, two daughter Hajera Begun, Anowara Khatun Piyara and wife Ayshon Bibi; Purchaser Tajem Ali died leaving one daughter Minara Begum, wife Maleka Begum, consanguine brother's son Adorn Ali and consanguine sister Sorbanu; Said Adorn Ali, Sorbanu, Ayesha Bibi, Hajera Bibi, Anowara Khatun and Minara Khatun sold 38 decimals of land to Plaintiff No.2 Moslem Ali Kha on 19.03.1973; Plaintiff No.2 Moslem Ali Kha transferred 10¾ of land to Defendant No.13 Shajahan; Plaintiff No.1 purchased 49½ decimals of land on 19.02.1982 and Plaintiff Nos.1 and 2 jointly purchased 80+22+42-144 decimals of land on 03.02.1985, 01.08.1987 and 02.03.1987 respectively; In this way plaintiffs' became owner and possessor of 4.41¼ of land of S.A. Khatian No.955 and 1.39 acres of land of S.A. Khatian No.954, in total 5.80¼ acres of land; Inspite of repeated requests of the plain-tiffs', the defendants refused to make amicable partition of the suit land which con-strained to file the suit for partition since there is no earlier partition by metes and bounds. 

 22. By now it is settled that the suit for partition is incompetent if all the co-sharers are not included as parties to the suit, as no effective decree can be passed in the absence of any one of them. It is true that under Order-I, Rule-9 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, no suit shall be defeated by reason of miss-joinder and non-joinder of parties but there can be no doubt that if the parties who are not joined are not only proper but also necessary parties to it the infirmity in the suit is bound to be fatal. 

 27. On perusal of record it appears that P. -01 admitted in his cross-examination that he doesn't know how much land there is in the former (sabek) plots and how much lands of the former (sabek) plots has been recorded in current (hal) plots. Again, the appellate court below on perusal of exhibit-2 and 2 (lea) arrived at a finding that the former (sabek) plot numbers of the current (hal) Plot Nos.2282 and 2285 are 96 and 909 respectively. The appellate court below also arrived at a finding that in the said exhibited docu-ment no former (sabek) plot number of current Plot No. 2284/2935 is mentioned. On perusal of plaint 2935 and exhibit-01 i.e. C.S. Khatian No.559 it appears that former Plot Nos.96 and 909 are not included in the schedule of the plaint as well as in the C.S. Khatian No.559. In this context appellate court below upon evidences on record arrived at a conclusive finding that the suit is barred by hutch-pot for non-inclusion of the land of former (sabek) Plot Nos.96 and 909 in the schedule of the plaint. Inspite of such finding of the appellate court below, the High Court Division did not utter a single word to controvert such finding of the appellate court below. 

 29. In the instant case, none of the above situations arose. So, there is no reason to deviate from the proposition of law settled by this Division.
